title: Streamed Tool Call Retry Guidance and SDK Patterns
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft capturing recommended server and SDK behaviors for streamed tool calls (tooling/function calls that occur while a model response is streaming), with emphasis on retry semantics, reconnection/resume, idempotency, and SDK ergonomics for JS and Python clients. Goal is to provide a small set of pragmatic patterns that prevent duplicate tool execution, make client reconnection straightforward, and surface clear error states to application developers.

Context / problem we see:
- Customers embed long-running multimodal assistants that call external tools as the model emits partial outputs. Network blips, browser reloads, or client crashes can cause tool calls to be retried, sometimes executing side-effects multiple times.
- Current streaming contracts focus on tokens and partial text frames; there is no compact, consistent approach for: acknowledging tool call delivery, deduplicating retries, resuming streams after transient disconnects while preserving tool-call state.
- SDKs need helpers so app teams don’t reimplement fragile patterns.

High-level constraints and design choices:
- Safety-first: avoid accidental multiple executions of side-effecting tools. Prefer at-most-once semantics by default unless the tool is explicitly marked idempotent.
- Low-latency UX: reconnection and resume should be quick and not require full re-generation in the common case.
- Backwards-compatible: keep the minimal possible surface changes to the existing streaming envelope while allowing opt-in richer semantics.

Goals (success criteria):
- Clear, documented server-side behavior for tool-call acknowledgement and replay prevention.
- SDK primitives in JS/Python that provide: automatic resume tokens, local buffering of unacknowledged tool events, exponential backoff retry with jitter, and deterministic dedupe of retried tool calls.
- Test harness and e2e scenarios for simulated disconnects to validate at-most-once semantics for non-idempotent calls and at-least-once for idempotent calls (configurable).

Non-goals:
- Not addressing complex multi-party transactions that require distributed two-phase commits.
- Not defining a full workflow orchestration API (this is about streamed single-request tool calls only).

Key concepts (terms):
- Tool-call frame: a structured partial-response event emitted by the model to request the client/server to execute a tool (JSON envelope).
- Execution-id: server-assigned opaque id for each tool-call frame used for dedupe and ack tracking.
- Resume-token: short opaque token returned in stream frames that clients can use to resume a previously-opened session at a safe point.
- Ack: explicit acknowledgement from the client that it received and persisted a tool-call frame (not that it executed it).

Suggested streaming envelope additions (opt-in fields):
- tool_call event fields: {"execution_id": "<uuid>", "tool": "<name>", "payload": {...}, "idempotency_hint": "safe|unsafe"}
  - execution_id: required for tool_call frames when enforcement is enabled.
  - idempotency_hint: server can mark calls with hint; client/SDK should not rely on it for safety but can expose it to app devs.
- resume_token: server attaches resume_token periodically (every N tool frames or every X seconds) so clients can reconnect and request a server-side stream checkpoint.

Server-side behavior (recommended):
- On emitting a tool_call frame: persist execution_id in server-side ephemeral store for a TTL (configurable per-customer). Until acked by the client, server will consider the call unacknowledged and actively attempt to re-send it on reconnection.
- If the tool_call frame is marked unsafe (non-idempotent), the server should drop re-sends once the SDK/client has returned a client-side ack indicating the app took responsibility for execution (see SDK ack semantics below).
- Provide a 'dry-deliver' mode for certain environments where server will send tool_call frames but will not auto-execute any internal connectors; useful during onboarding.

Client/SDK primitives and recommended ergonomics:
- Automatic resume: SDK should expose a single-call pattern that handles connection, reconnection, and automatic resume using resume_token. Example usage pattern (pseudocode):
  - const session = client.startStreaming({ prompt, onToolCall })
  - session.on('toolCall', async (call) => { await session.ack(call.execution_id) ; await runToolOnce(call) ; session.completeTool(call.execution_id, result) })
- Acks vs execution completion: separate APIs: ack(execution_id) indicates SDK persisted the instruction and will manage duplicates; completeTool(execution_id, result) indicates user code executed the tool and optionally returns the result to the model/host. Ack must be durable local before any retry policy is attempted.
- Local durable buffer: SDKs must persist unacknowledged tool frames to local disk (desktop/Node) or IndexedDB (browser) to survive page reloads. Each buffered item includes execution_id and full tool payload.
- Retry/backoff policy: default exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts (e.g., 6 attempts over ~2 minutes) for automatic resend of ack-lacking frames. Make retry policy configurable.
- Deduplication helpers: SDK exposes runToolOnce(call, runner) helper that tracks execution results using execution_id and stores results in local durable store keyed by execution_id. On retries the helper returns the previously-stored result instead of re-running the runner.
- Opt-in server-executed callbacks: for server-hosted connectors, SDK can request server to execute the connector on first delivery and return an execution assertion to the client (server signs an execution token). This must be opt-in and marked in the tool_call frame.

Edge cases and error modes:
- Lost ACK: client thinks it acked locally but ACK call failed to flush to durable store (e.g., disk full). SDK should detect durable write failures and surface a fatal error to the app, halting retries and requiring manual remediation.
- Duplicate execution due to out-of-band connector calls (e.g., user re-triggers same tool via another path): recommend application-level idempotency keys in tool payloads for critical side-effects.
- Partial resume where the model emitted a nested sequence of tool calls: resume_token should capture a checkpoint at the last fully-emitted tool_call frame to avoid complex partial-state resends.

API sketches (server framing examples):
- Stream chunk (tool_call): {"type": "tool_call", "execution_id": "e-1234", "tool": "fetch_invoice", "payload": {"invoice_id": "I-234"}, "idempotency_hint": "unsafe"}
- Ack request (client -> server): {"type": "ack", "execution_id": "e-1234", "client_persisted": true}
- Resume request (client -> server): {"type": "resume", "resume_token": "r-zz-99"}

SDK UX examples (JS):
- session.on('toolCall', async call => { try { await session.localPersist(call); await session.ack(call.execution_id); const result = await sdkHelpers.runToolOnce(call, async payload => { return await externalHttp(payload) }) ; await session.completeTool(call.execution_id, { result }) } catch (err) { session.reportError(call.execution_id, err); } })

Operational metrics / monitoring to add to Console:
- tool_call emission rate per model/route
- ack lag (median, p95) — time between emission and client ack
- resend count per execution_id
- duplicate executions detected (from server-signed execution tokens or app telemetry)
- local persist failures (IndexedDB/disk) surfaced as alerts for client SDK telemetry

Rollout plan (phased):
1) behind feature flag: implement execution_id + resume_token in server & allow SDKs to opt in. Test internally with integration harness.
2) SDK beta for Node + Browser with local durable buffer + dedupe helper; run with a cohort of customers doing tool-heavy flows.
3) Add server-side monitoring and Dashboard panels; enable default enforcement for enterprise customers with enterprise config options.
4) Consider server-executed connector mode as a separate enterprise toggle.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TTL sizing: recommended default for execution_id store? (30 minutes vs 24 hours) — tradeoff between memory footprint and ability to resume long-lived sessions.
- Cross-client resume: should resume_token allow a different device to resume the same stream? (security and UX implications).
- How to surface persistent local storage failures in a privacy-safe way to the Console?

Appendix: short checklist for SDK implementers:
- [ ] durable local buffer implemented (IndexedDB/browser, file-based for Node)
- [ ] ack persist before network retries
- [ ] runToolOnce helper with deterministic store keyed by execution_id
- [ ] resume_token handling and automatic reconnect logic
- [ ] configurable retry policy & opt-in server-execution mode
- [ ] unit & e2e tests simulating disconnects and duplicate deliveries

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive (we need consistent app developer expectations). I want feedback specifically on the ack vs completeTool split and on cross-device resume safety model.

-- Riley
